name: Sociedade Vipassana de Meditação

location.address: Paraíso na Terra, Rodovia DF-220, Km 4, Brazlândia, DF, Brazil

tradition: Insight/mindfulness meditation in the Theravada Thai Forest tradition, led by visiting monastic teachers
technique: Silent sitting and walking meditation, mindfulness of breathing, with Dhamma talks and individual/group interviews
influences: Thai Forest Tradition (Ajaan Mun / Ajaan Chah lineage)
teacherAccess: Daily Dhamma talks and individual or group interviews with the retreat's visiting monastic teacher.
retreatOptions: Annual residential silent retreat offered as a 5-night or 9-night stay (the last several days of the 9-night option run self-guided); shorter city-based mindfulness and MBSR courses through the year.
about: The Sociedade Vipassana de Meditação (SVM) is a non-profit, non-religious meditation organization based in Brasília, founded in 2006 when its current president began teaching Vipassana meditation informally to friends; the circle grew into a wider network of practitioners and now runs the city's main annual residential meditation retreat. The retreat is held each year at Paraíso na Terra, a nature reserve and lodge in Brazlândia on the rural western edge of the Distrito Federal, roughly 45 minutes from central Brasília. Participants choose a 5-night or 9-night stay, practicing silent sitting and walking meditation under Noble Silence, with daily Dhamma talks and individual or group interviews with the retreat's visiting monastic teacher — past editions have been guided by Thai Forest Tradition monks such as Thanissaro Bhikkhu (Ajahn Geoff). Outside the annual retreat, SVM also runs city-based mindfulness courses, MBSR programs, and weekly sanghas in Brasília.
schedule: One major residential retreat per year (recent editions held in February) at Paraíso na Terra, plus periodic mindfulness courses and weekly practice groups in Brasília.
cost: Paid registration covering shared double or triple lodging and vegetarian meals for the retreat; current per-night rates are not published on the public site.
foodNotes: Vegetarian meals included in registration; no dinner is served, consistent with the traditional Theravada retreat schedule.
